title: Genesis Journey selected-episode coverage inventory
scope: Source-level inventory of selected Journey episodes and exact remaining verse intervals across all 50 Genesis chapters. It is not a claim that every verse or chapter is illustrated, and it is not live runtime acceptance.

method.catalog_ranges: The consolidated passage-scenes.json scene ranges determine when a catalog scene is selected; they are counted even where no dedicated hotspot exists.
method.hotspot_ranges: Each hotspot active range, source range, title, and anchor is recorded independently. Scene-range verses without a dedicated hotspot are flagged.
method.legacy_eden: The broad symbolic Eden fallback intervals are documented as contextual routing only. Only exact currently effective stop anchors are added to the selected-reference ledger; Genesis 3:23–24 are shadowed by the newer catalog scene.
method.legacy_flood: Visible flood story phases are included from the current legacy stop definitions, which cover Genesis 7–8. The catalog bow scene selects Genesis 9:12–17; Genesis 9:1–11 remains unillustrated at episode level.
method.unillustrated_intervals: Exact complement against the verse counts in the local King James Version corpus, after selected scene ranges and exact legacy Eden stop anchors are combined. Broad contextual routing does not count as episode illustration.

summary.live_runtime_acceptance: NOT RUN in this inventory task

catalog_scenes.title: Abraham welcomes the visitors and Sarah hears the promise
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 18:1–15

hotspots.title: Abraham welcomes the visitors
hotspots.note: Abraham runs to meet the three men and offers water, rest, and food. The visible visitors help explain the welcome described in Genesis 18:2–5.

hotspots.title: Abraham serves the meal
hotspots.note: Sarah prepares cakes, a young man prepares the calf, and Abraham serves butter, milk, and the prepared calf beneath the tree. He stands by the visitors while they eat.

hotspots.title: Sarah hears the promise
hotspots.note: Sarah hears from the tent door that she will have a son. She laughs within herself because of their age, and the Lord questions her response. The doorway matters because she listens there.

catalog_scenes.title: The pledge Judah gives
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated object study · Genesis 38:18 · Object forms are reconstructed

hotspots.title: The pledge that identifies Judah
hotspots.note: Tamar asks for Judah’s signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge. Later, these objects identify him. This object study illustrates their role without depicting the encounter described in the verse.

hotspots.title: Tamar sends the evidence
hotspots.note: Tamar sends word to Judah, asking him to recognize the signet, bracelets, and staff. These are the objects he gave as a pledge earlier in the chapter.

hotspots.title: Judah acknowledges his failure
hotspots.note: Judah recognizes the objects and acknowledges his failure to give Tamar to Shelah his son. The illustration focuses on his recognition and admission.

catalog_scenes.title: Dry land, seas, and seed-bearing plants
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 1:9–13

hotspots.title: Waters gathered into seas
hotspots.note: Genesis names the gathered waters Seas. The water is a visible subject for that verse; this coastline is an illustration, not a proposed location.

hotspots.title: Dry land appears
hotspots.note: The passage distinguishes dry land from the gathered waters and calls the dry land Earth. The marker identifies the visible shore rather than an invented travel stop.

hotspots.title: Plants and fruit bearing seed
hotspots.note: The text names grass, herbs yielding seed, and fruit trees whose seed is in their fruit. The species pictured are illustrative and are not identified in Genesis.

catalog_scenes.title: Clothed and sent out from the garden
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 3:21–24

hotspots.title: Clothed and sent out
hotspots.note: After the garments of skins are made, the man is sent out of the garden to till the ground. The illustration includes the clothed couple departing; their appearance and clothing construction are not specified in the text.

hotspots.title: The guarded way
hotspots.note: Cherubim and a flaming sword guard the way to the tree of life. Genesis does not describe the cherubim as the winged human figures shown here; that form is an artistic convention.

catalog_scenes.title: Cain and Abel bring their offerings
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 4:3–5

hotspots.title: Cain’s fruit of the ground
hotspots.note: Cain brings an offering from the fruit of the ground. The basket makes that offering visible; its particular crops and container are artistic choices.

hotspots.title: Abel’s firstlings of the flock
hotspots.note: Abel brings firstlings of his flock and their fat. The living lamb illustrates bringing an offering, not the full sacrificial act. The passage describes the Lord’s regard; no visible supernatural signal is invented here.

catalog_scenes.title: Noah prepares the ark
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 6:14–16, 22 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Build with wood
hotspots.note: The command specifies gopher wood, rooms, and dimensions. The wood species and exact ark form cannot be established from this reconstruction.

hotspots.title: Pitch within and without
hotspots.note: Noah applies dark pitch to the wooden side. Genesis names pitch inside and outside; the tool and pot are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: A door in the side
hotspots.note: The visible opening illustrates the door placed in the ark's side. Genesis also describes a window and three stories.

catalog_scenes.title: The bow in the cloud
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 9:12–17 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: The bow in the cloud
hotspots.note: God names the bow in the cloud as the token of the covenant between himself and the earth. The rainbow is the visible subject.

hotspots.title: Every living creature
hotspots.note: The covenant includes every living creature. The sheep and cattle represent living creatures; this animal grouping is illustrative.

catalog_scenes.title: Bricks for a city and tower
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 11:3–4 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Brick and mortar
hotspots.note: The builders make fired bricks and use slime for mortar. The visible reddish brick and dark mortar illustrate those materials.

hotspots.title: A city and tower
hotspots.note: The people propose a city and a tower to make themselves a name. Its stepped shape and scaffolding are reconstructed.

catalog_scenes.title: Abram departs with his household
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 12:4–5 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Abram, Sarai, and Lot depart
hotspots.note: Abram leaves Haran with Sarai his wife and Lot his brother's son. The visible travelers illustrate the departure; their appearance is reconstructed.

hotspots.title: They take their possessions
hotspots.note: The household takes its gathered substance and people. The loaded pack animal represents those possessions without establishing an exact inventory or route.

catalog_scenes.title: Abram and Lot separate
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 13:8–12 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Let there be no strife
hotspots.note: Abram urges Lot to avoid strife and offers him the choice of land. The open-hand conversation illustrates this peaceful separation.

hotspots.title: Lot takes his household toward the plain
hotspots.note: Lot chooses the well-watered plain, journeys east, and pitches his tent toward Sodom. The tent and flock identify a moving household; their screen position is not a geographic bearing.

catalog_scenes.title: Melchizedek brings bread and wine
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 14:18–19 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Melchizedek brings bread and wine
hotspots.note: The bread and wine vessel illustrate what Melchizedek brings forth as king of Salem and priest of the most high God.

hotspots.title: Melchizedek blesses Abram
hotspots.note: Melchizedek blesses Abram in the name of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth. The raised hand represents his spoken blessing.

catalog_scenes.title: Abram looks toward the stars
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 15:5–6 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Abram looks toward heaven
hotspots.note: Abram is brought outside and told to look toward heaven. He believes the LORD; the visible man illustrates Abram's attention, while the text conveys his faith.

hotspots.title: Number the stars
hotspots.note: The stars illustrate the comparison given for Abram's seed. Their pattern is artistic and does not identify an exact ancient sky.

catalog_scenes.title: Hagar beside the wilderness fountain
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 16:7–8, 13–14 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Hagar is found in the wilderness
hotspots.note: The angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a fountain and asks where she has come from and where she is going. The illustration shows Hagar; the speaker remains unseen.

hotspots.title: The fountain and the named well
hotspots.note: Hagar speaks of the God who sees her, and the well is named Beer-lahai-roi. The visible water identifies this setting without claiming its exact geography or construction.

catalog_scenes.title: Lot escapes toward Zoar
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 19:22–24 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Lot enters Zoar at sunrise
hotspots.note: Lot is urged to escape to Zoar and enters when the sun has risen. The visible man entering the gate represents Lot; the gate and companions' appearance are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah
hotspots.note: Genesis describes brimstone and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah. The distant burning cities illustrate this non-graphically; their location relative to Zoar is an editorial composition.

catalog_scenes.title: Sarah is restored to Abraham
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 20:14, 16 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

hotspots.title: Sarah is restored to Abraham
hotspots.note: Abimelech restores Sarah to Abraham. The visible couple illustrates her return; faces, clothing, and the setting are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Sheep and oxen are given
hotspots.note: Sheep and oxen are among the gifts Abimelech gives Abraham. The visible animals represent those gifts; the attendants are shown with dignity.

hotspots.title: The gift of silver
hotspots.note: Abimelech tells Sarah of the silver he has given. The bowl represents silver pieces without claiming an exact ancient form or counting the thousand named in the verse.

catalog_scenes.title: Hagar sees a well and gives Ishmael water
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 21:14–19

hotspots.title: Hagar fills the bottle
hotspots.note: After God opens her eyes to a well, Hagar fills the water bottle and gives the lad a drink. The visible vessel represents the bottle named in the passage.

hotspots.title: The lad drinks
hotspots.note: God hears the lad where he is and promises Hagar that he will become a great nation. His drinking here depicts the rescue in verse 19; his appearance is imagined.

catalog_scenes.title: Abraham sees the ram caught in the thicket
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 22:9–14

hotspots.title: The altar and wood
hotspots.note: Abraham builds an altar and arranges the wood. The visible stone construction is an illustrative choice.

hotspots.title: The ram in the thicket
hotspots.note: Abraham sees a ram caught by its horns and offers it instead of his son. The image selects the living ram before the offering.

hotspots.title: Abraham and Isaac
hotspots.note: The angel calls from heaven to stop Abraham, and Isaac is spared. Their safe stance is an editorial reconstruction; no heavenly speaker is pictured.

catalog_scenes.title: Abraham weighs silver for the field and cave
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 23:16–20

hotspots.title: Four hundred shekels of silver
hotspots.note: Abraham weighs the agreed silver to Ephron in the hearing of the sons of Heth. The balance and silver pieces visualize weighing; their number and form are not an archaeological claim.

hotspots.title: The cave in the field
hotspots.note: The field and its cave become Abraham's possession for a burial place. Verse 19 places Machpelah before Mamre, identified as Hebron; this cave's appearance is imagined.

hotspots.title: The witnessed purchase
hotspots.note: Ephron receives the named price, and the purchase is made secure before the children of Heth. Their placement beside the cave is an editorial condensation.

catalog_scenes.title: Rebekah draws water for the servant's camels
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 24:15–20

hotspots.title: Rebekah and her pitcher
hotspots.note: Rebekah comes with a pitcher, gives the servant a drink, and then empties water into the trough for his camels.

hotspots.title: Water for the camels
hotspots.note: She offers to draw water until all the camels have finished drinking. The visible camel and trough show that act of hospitality.

hotspots.title: Abraham's travelling servant
hotspots.note: The servant asks for a little water from her pitcher. She serves him before offering water for the animals; the illustration selects the later moment.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob gives Esau bread and lentil stew
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 25:29–34

hotspots.title: Red lentil pottage
hotspots.note: Esau returns faint from the field and asks for the red pottage. After his oath, Jacob gives him bread and lentil stew.

hotspots.title: Jacob asks for the birthright
hotspots.note: Jacob asks Esau to sell his birthright that day and to swear to the agreement. The visible handover condenses that exchange.

hotspots.title: Esau chooses the meal
hotspots.note: Esau says the birthright will not profit him as he feels near death, then eats, drinks and leaves. Verse 34 says he despised his birthright.

hotspots.title: The new well
hotspots.note: Isaac moves and digs another well, for which they do not strive. The visible water and well stand for Rehoboth, not a composite of all three wells.

hotspots.title: Isaac gives thanks for room
hotspots.note: Isaac calls the well Rehoboth and says the Lord has made room for them to be fruitful in the land. His gesture is illustrative; no divine figure is depicted.

hotspots.title: Water after the digging
hotspots.note: Isaac's servants find springing water, and successive disputes lead to the final uncontested well. The servant's water bucket is a reconstruction of the work, not a tool specified in these verses.

catalog_scenes.title: Isaac feels Jacob's hands and blesses him
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 27:22–29

hotspots.title: The hands Isaac feels
hotspots.note: Isaac says the voice is Jacob's but the hands are Esau's, and he does not discern him because the hands are hairy. Jacob claims to be Esau.

hotspots.title: Isaac blesses his son
hotspots.note: Isaac asks his son to come near and kiss him, then speaks a blessing of provision and rule. The illustration selects the touch earlier in this sequence.

hotspots.title: The meal and wine
hotspots.note: Jacob brings food for Isaac to eat and wine to drink. The tableware and presentation shown here are imagined.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 28:10–19

hotspots.title: Jacob rests for the night
hotspots.note: On his way toward Haran, Jacob stops after sunset, takes stones for pillows and lies down to sleep.

hotspots.title: The ladder in the dream
hotspots.note: Jacob dreams of a ladder set on the earth whose top reaches heaven. Its luminous appearance is an artistic way to distinguish the dream from the surrounding landscape.

hotspots.title: Angels ascend and descend
hotspots.note: The dream includes angels of God ascending and descending on the ladder. Wings, robes and faces are illustrative choices, not descriptions supplied by this verse.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob meets Rachel and waters her flock
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 29:9–12

hotspots.title: Jacob waters the flock
hotspots.note: Jacob rolls the stone from the well's mouth and waters the flock belonging to Laban, his mother's brother. The bucket is an illustrative detail.

hotspots.title: Rachel comes with the sheep
hotspots.note: Rachel keeps her father's sheep and comes with them to the well. The visible flock explains the purpose of the watering.

hotspots.title: The stone moved from the mouth
hotspots.note: The text specifically says Jacob rolls the stone away. The large stone beside the well represents that action; its size and shape are imagined.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob sets peeled rods before the watering flocks
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 30:37–43

hotspots.title: White stripes in the rods
hotspots.note: Jacob peels white streaks into rods and places them before the flocks in the watering gutters and troughs. The visible bark and exposed wood make that detail recognizable.

hotspots.title: The flocks at the trough
hotspots.note: The flocks come to drink before the rods; the account describes ringstraked, speckled and spotted offspring and Jacob separating the lambs. The image selects animals drinking, without depicting mating or birth.

hotspots.title: Jacob manages the flocks
hotspots.note: Jacob keeps his own flocks apart and distinguishes stronger and feebler animals in the narrated practice. Verse 43 describes his increase in animals and servants.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob and Laban make a covenant by the stone heap
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 31:44–52

hotspots.title: The heap is a witness
hotspots.note: Jacob's kin gather stones into a heap. Laban calls the heap a witness and says neither party is to pass it toward the other for harm.

hotspots.title: Jacob sets up a pillar
hotspots.note: Jacob takes a stone and sets it up as a pillar. Its upright shape here is illustrative rather than a record of the original memorial.

hotspots.title: The covenant between Jacob and Laban
hotspots.note: Laban proposes a covenant. The agreement includes concern for his daughters and a boundary against harm. The open-handed poses are an imagined way to depict their solemn exchange.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob wrestles until the breaking of day
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 32:24–30

hotspots.title: Jacob holds on
hotspots.note: Jacob is left alone and wrestles until daybreak. When told to let go, he says he will not do so unless he is blessed. The image avoids depicting the injury in verse 25.

hotspots.title: The man and the blessing
hotspots.note: The man asks Jacob's name, names him Israel, and blesses him. He does not supply his own name. Verse 30 records Jacob's words about seeing God; the illustration adds no halo, wings or divine portrait.

hotspots.title: Esau embraces Jacob
hotspots.note: Esau runs to meet Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck, kisses him, and they weep.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 35:6–7

hotspots.title: Jacob at Bethel
hotspots.note: Jacob comes to Luz, also called Bethel, with the people accompanying him.

hotspots.title: The altar
hotspots.note: Jacob builds an altar and calls the place El-beth-el, remembering where God appeared to him when he fled from his brother.

hotspots.title: Joseph's coat
hotspots.note: Israel loves Joseph more than his other children and makes him a coat of many colours.

hotspots.title: The brothers' response
hotspots.note: The brothers see their father's special love for Joseph and hate him; they cannot speak peaceably to him. Their visible expressions are interpretive.

catalog_scenes.title: The garment Joseph leaves behind
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated object study · Genesis 39:12–13 · Garment and setting reconstructed

hotspots.title: The left garment
hotspots.note: Joseph leaves his garment in her hand and flees outside. The next verse again notes that he has left the garment and gone.

hotspots.title: The vine and ripe grapes
hotspots.note: In the dream a vine stands before the cupbearer. Its three branches bud, blossom and bring forth ripe grapes. The image concentrates on the ripe grapes rather than proving a precise branch count.

hotspots.title: Grapes pressed into the cup
hotspots.note: The cupbearer takes the grapes, presses them into Pharaoh's cup and gives the cup to Pharaoh. The cup's form is reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Pharaoh's ring
hotspots.note: Pharaoh takes his ring from his hand and puts it on Joseph's hand. Its exact design is reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Fine linen and a gold chain
hotspots.note: Joseph is arrayed in fine linen and given a gold chain about his neck. These visible objects are named in the verse; their styling is interpretive.

hotspots.title: The brothers bow
hotspots.note: Joseph's brothers come and bow before him with their faces to the earth.

hotspots.title: Joseph recognizes them
hotspots.note: Joseph recognizes his brothers and conceals his identity. Their failure to recognize him is part of the narrative, not something a still image can prove.

hotspots.title: Benjamin's portion
hotspots.note: Joseph sends portions from before him. Benjamin's portion is five times as much as any of the others, and they drink and are merry with him.

hotspots.title: Joseph eats separately
hotspots.note: The food is set for Joseph by himself, for the brothers by themselves, and for the Egyptians separately. The background table makes Joseph's separation visible.

catalog_scenes.title: The silver cup in Benjamin's sack
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated object study · Genesis 44:1–2, 12–13

hotspots.title: Joseph's silver cup
hotspots.note: Joseph commands the steward to put his silver cup in the youngest brother's sack. The search later finds the cup in Benjamin's sack.

hotspots.title: Food and money in the sack
hotspots.note: The steward is told to fill the sacks with food and put every man's money in the sack's mouth. The plain metal pieces are interpretive; Genesis does not specify their shape.

hotspots.title: Joseph and Benjamin weep
hotspots.note: Joseph falls upon Benjamin's neck and weeps, and Benjamin weeps upon his neck.

hotspots.title: His brothers gather near
hotspots.note: Joseph kisses all his brothers and weeps upon them. Afterward they talk with him. The still image gathers them around the central embrace.

hotspots.title: Jacob and the household in wagons
hotspots.note: The sons of Israel carry Jacob their father, their little ones and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh sent.

hotspots.title: Cattle and goods accompany them
hotspots.note: They take the cattle and goods acquired in Canaan and come into Egypt, with Jacob's descendants accompanying him.

catalog_scenes.title: Joseph supplies food in exchange for livestock
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 47:15–17

hotspots.title: Joseph supplies food
hotspots.note: The Egyptians come to Joseph when money fails. He tells them to bring their cattle, and he will give them food in exchange.

hotspots.title: Livestock exchanged for food
hotspots.note: Joseph gives food in exchange for horses, flocks, cattle and asses. The visible goat represents the flocks; one animal does not stand for an exact price or quantity.

catalog_scenes.title: Jacob crosses his hands to bless the boys
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 48:13–16

hotspots.title: Jacob deliberately crosses his hands
hotspots.note: Israel places his right hand upon Ephraim's head and his left upon Manasseh's, guiding his hands deliberately even though Manasseh is firstborn. Ephraim is shown at the viewer's right.

hotspots.title: The blessing of the lads
hotspots.note: Jacob calls on the God who fed him throughout his life and asks that the lads be blessed, bear the family name, and grow into a multitude. The invoked Angel is not pictured.

hotspots.title: A lion as a comparison for Judah
hotspots.note: Jacob calls Judah a lion's whelp and describes him stooping and couching as a lion. The visible animal represents this literary comparison; Judah is not literally an animal in the narrative.

catalog_scenes.title: Joseph is placed in a coffin in Egypt
catalog_scenes.caption: Illustrated object study · Genesis 50:26 · Coffin form reconstructed

hotspots.title: The coffin in Egypt
hotspots.note: Joseph dies at the age of 110. He is embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt. The verse does not specify the coffin's exact design.

catalog_scenes.title: Families of Noah’s sons
catalog_scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 10:1–6, 21–22 · not geography, chronology, or a complete genealogy

hotspots.title: Noah and his sons
hotspots.note: The root and three son branches are visible in the diagram; the anchor is the passage that names the family.

hotspots.title: Japheth’s family
hotspots.note: The named sons of Japheth and selected Gomer/Javan descendants appear as text. The note for verse 5 avoids drawing borders or assigning modern peoples.

hotspots.title: Ham’s sons
hotspots.note: The four sons named in verse 6 are listed beneath Ham.

hotspots.title: Shem and his named children
hotspots.note: The diagram states the Eber-descendant relation in verse 21 separately and lists the children named in verse 22; it does not add intervening branches.

catalog_scenes.title: Names and a promised son
catalog_scenes.coverage_label: Genesis 17:5, 15, 19–21 · names and future promise only
catalog_scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 17:5, 15, 19–21 · not a map, timeline, birth scene, or full chapter

hotspots.title: Abram is named Abraham
hotspots.note: Both names and the name-giving reference are visible in the diagram.

hotspots.title: Sarai is named Sarah
hotspots.note: Both names and the name-giving reference are visible in the diagram.

hotspots.title: Isaac is promised to Sarah and Abraham
hotspots.note: Isaac is labeled as promised for the future, with the selected promise range. No birth scene is shown.

catalog_scenes.title: Family relationships and response
catalog_scenes.caption: Relationship diagram · Genesis 34:1, 25, 30–31 · not a map, timeline, or full chapter; no assault or retaliation illustration

hotspots.title: Dinah, daughter of Leah and Jacob
hotspots.note: The two parent links and Dinah’s name are visible; the relationship follows the selected verse.

hotspots.title: Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers
hotspots.note: The text names the brothers and identifies them as Jacob’s sons; the diagram shows the sibling relationship without the violent act.

hotspots.title: Jacob and his sons’ exchange
hotspots.note: The diagram marks the response and reply as a text relationship; it does not illustrate the retaliation.

catalog_scenes.title: Esau and his named family
catalog_scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 36:1–5 · selected family, not a map, timeline, or full chapter

hotspots.title: Esau, who is Edom
hotspots.note: The name Edom is associated with Esau in the selected verse.

hotspots.title: Esau’s named wives
hotspots.note: The three named wives are shown with their references; the diagram does not invent additional family details.

hotspots.title: Sons through the named mothers
hotspots.note: The diagram connects Eliphaz, Reuel, and the sons of Aholibamah to the mothers named in the selected verses.
